Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Household, washing & chores

supply noun

a stock of something; supplies

also supplies, stock, provisions, a supply of, stores, provision

classical

Caes. BC 1.49: exercitus omnium rērum abundābat cōpiā (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 71: bonōrum memoria et cōpia

cōpia, cōpiae f.

noun, first declension

a supply, a stock, plenty (of something)

With the genitive of what there is a supply of; in the plural, cōpiae, supplies and resources (see resources).

Other words

  • commeātus, commeātūs m. — supplies, provisions (for an army or a journey)

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Traupman 188, 388; Caes. BG 2.9: commeātū nostrōs prohibēre (Lewis & Short)

    Traupman: used both as a collective singular and in the plural.

Examples

  • frūctus autem senectūtis est, ut saepe dīxī, ante partōrum bonōrum memoria et cōpia

    the harvest of old age, as I have often said, is the memory and the store of good things gathered beforeCic. Sen. 71

See also provide, store, resources.

SourcesLewis & Short: copia · Lewis & Short: commeatus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 188, 388, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
